mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined every week for four consecutive weeks (-20.9 to -47.1). This trajectory reflects inertial adaptation of consumer routines to a lower mobility baseline; absent any reversal signal, the downward trend will mechanically persist into the next four weeks because behavioral adjustment to reduced movement is gradual and self-reinforcing.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from -20.9 to -47.1 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days rises above its mean over the last 28 days despite the uninterrupted four-week decline observed, the trend-persistence mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week WORKPLACES drop exceeding 15 points, as occurred from t-1w (-39.1) to t-0w (-54.9), signals a fresh wave of business-closure policy enforcement. This policy shock suppresses retail footfall in the immediate following week as both employees and shoppers curtail non-essential trips in response to the new restriction regime.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -39.1 at t-1w to -54.9 at t-0w, a 15.8-point drop
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 7 days does not fall following a WORKPLACES week-on-week drop exceeding 15 points, the policy-shock transmission hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (9.0 to 22.3) combined with sharply falling TRANSIT mobility (-35.3 to -64.9) indicates households are jointly substituting home-based activity for out-of-home movement while losing transit access. The compounded co-movement of these two series predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT falls concurrently across two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.0 to 22.3 while TRANSIT fell from -35.3 to -64.9 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 14 days does not decline despite concurrent RESIDENTIAL increase and TRANSIT decrease, the joint sheltering-and-access-loss mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The partial rebound in PARKS mobility from -42.1 at t-1w to -35.7 at t-0w suggests an emerging seasonal or weather-driven pull toward outdoor recreation. Under a regime of easing weather constraints, this outdoor substitution effect diverts discretionary trips away from indoor retail and recreation venues, pressuring RETAIL_REC downward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC remains flat or declining
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -42.1 at t-1w to -35.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 14 days rises concurrently with continued PARKS improvement, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, GROCERY_PHARM's decline from +15.1 at t-3w to -15.1 at t-0w signals that even essential shopping trips are being curtailed, indicating enforcement has broadened beyond non-essential retail categories. This broadened restriction depth foreshadows further four-week declines in RETAIL_REC as overall mobility suppression deepens.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from +15.1 at t-3w to -15.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days stabilizes or rises while GROCERY_PHARM remains negative or continues falling, the broadened-restriction-depth hypothesis is rejected.

This joint, compounded reduction accelerates the near-term decline of RETAIL_REC over the following week beyond the effect of either series alone.

failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a joint drop exceeding 20 points in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the compounded-access-reduction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The monotonic rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 9.0 to 22.3 reflects an entrenching behavioral shift toward home-centric living. As this trend continues independent of any specific external trigger, it will continue to crowd out retail and recreation trips over the next four weeks regardless of other mobility signals.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 9.0 to 22.3 across the four observed weeks

If this parks rebound persists alongside stabilizing WORKPLACES, it signals an imminent loosening of restrictions that will lift RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as retail venues reopen in tandem.
